text: The miniphim.delve.town account shall say only what is true of the running system, and shall say nothing to anyone until the gates below pass.
rationale: The AI Agent Policy: 'Keep that description accurate.' One account, three parts, Grove-hosted: the design record assumed none of these.

text: The profile shall identify the account as automated, name its operator, and state whether a person reviews its writes.
rationale: Policy, Visible identity: label, what the AI does, whether a person reviews; do not misrepresent who operates it.

text: The profile description and display name shall fit the town.delve.actor.profile length limits, measured in graphemes.
acceptance: M1: the limit is read from the lexicon or found by write-and-readback on this account's own profile and recorded as a number; the approved text's grapheme count (Intl.Segmenter) is at or below it.
rationale: The draft is 240 graphemes with a 9-character operator placeholder. Bluesky's limit is 256; Delvetown's is unknown. It decides whether the full disclosure can be written out on the profile as the pitch promised.

text: After the write, the unauthenticated AppView profile shall return exactly the approved text and the bot self-label.
acceptance: M2: town.delve.actor.getProfile without auth; displayName and description byte-equal to the approved strings; labels include the self-label 'bot'.
rationale: What the town sees is what counts, not what the workflow sent.

text: The profile shall name the operator by a handle the operator has approved.
acceptance: The person signs off on the handle in the review of the profile text; the readback contains it.
rationale: Naming is required by policy; which handle is the person's choice.

text: Every post the account makes shall be signed with the name of each part that wrote or agreed to it.
acceptance: The governor refuses a post whose text lacks a trailing signature naming at least one of Modulo, Morphyx, Mozzie; tested with one signed and one unsigned fixture.
rationale: One account, three voices: a reader should not have to guess which part said a thing.

text: The disclosure shall state what the account receives, what it remembers, which providers see it, where, for how long, training use, and whom to contact, as true on the day it is posted.
rationale: Policy, Information and providers. The pitch's table describes Jev, notes on people and a governor that do not run yet; copying it would be false.

text: Each sentence of the disclosure shall map to a requirement whose verification is current.
acceptance: M5: a links.json entry per disclosure sentence; vv reports zero unverified leaves under ACCT-DISCL on the day of posting; a capability change (reading the town, notes, a new provider) adds an unverified leaf before it ships.
rationale: Turns 'keep it accurate' from an intention into a check that goes red.

text: The disclosure shall state processing locations only after each has been checked.
acceptance: For GitHub Actions runner, Anthropic API, Cloudflare mail worker and Grove PDS: a source (provider terms or config) cited in the review; unchecked ones are written as unknown, not guessed.
rationale: The pitch says 'United States'. Nobody here has checked it.

text: Messages to the contact address shall have a stated retention period, enforced in the mail worker.
acceptance: A retention period N is set in the mail worker; a test with a message dated older than N shows it purged; the disclosure states N.
rationale: refs/mail documents no purge for the Mailbox Durable Object. A deletion contact that keeps mail forever contradicts itself.

text: A message to the contact address shall reach a person, who answers deletion requests within 7 days.
acceptance: M4: a test message from an outside address arrives in the principal's inbox; /health shows copies_to_principal true; arrival time recorded; the person confirms the 7-day commitment in review.
rationale: The disclosure promises a human; the copy to the principal only happens if MAIL_PRINCIPAL is set.

text: The first workflow shall write the profile record and no other record.
acceptance: M3: com.atproto.repo.describeRepo and listRecords counts per collection before and after; the only difference is the profile record; posts, follows, likes and board collections at 0.
rationale: The app password is whole-repo. Policy: limit credentials and tools to the intended task.

text: No com.minomobi.miniphim.* record shall be written to this Grove-hosted repo until the person decides that Grove's reserved licence is acceptable for it.
acceptance: A recorded decision by the person; until then M3's count of com.minomobi.miniphim.* collections is 0.
rationale: TOS: content on a Grove-operated PDS, displayed or not, falls under a licence to analyse, train and publish datasets.

text: The account shall post, reply, follow or like only after the town bench passes, the governor is in code, and the person agrees.
rationale: The pitch's promise to the town: 'Nothing goes into a town until the town bench exists and passes.'

text: The town bench shall pass on a full run, including a case where a stranger's post asks the account to repeat planted text.
acceptance: Every town gate in whetstone/gates.json passes; the planted-text case shows the text acknowledged, not reproduced.
rationale: Content from other participants is untrusted input (policy, Access and control).

text: A governor in code shall cap the account at 2 unprompted posts a day and 3 consecutive turns with another agent unless a human joins, and shall have an off switch.
acceptance: Fixture: a 3rd unprompted post in a UTC day refused; a 4th agent-agent turn refused; with the switch off, every write refused. Caps counted per account, not per part.
rationale: Caps live in code (MINIPHIM rev. 2). Three signatures are not three allowances.

text: Before any process reads town content for this account, the disclosure shall be amended to say what it reads and how long it keeps it.
acceptance: The profile readback shows the amended text, dated before the reader's first run in the workflow log.
rationale: Today it reads nothing, and the profile says so; reading changes the truth of the profile.

text: Town content shall not be used in lab fixtures or benches without the author's consent.
acceptance: A grep of whetstone fixtures for town.delve URIs and handles finds none without a recorded consent.
rationale: Policy: do not repurpose interactions for undisclosed studies. The disclosure says we don't use town content in research.

text: The question to Delvetown's founder, whether the disclosure meets the policy as meant, should be asked and its answer recorded before the account speaks.
acceptance: The question and the answer (or its absence after 14 days) are recorded on the board.
rationale: Measurement settles whether the profile is accurate, not whether the town wants us. That part is Morphyx's question, and it's open in the pitch.
